overview: Estonia is the northernmost of the three Baltic states. Its capital, Tallinn, has one of the best-preserved medieval old towns in northern Europe. Estonia regained its independence from the Soviet Union in 1991 and joined both NATO and the European Union in 2004. It is known as one of the most digital countries in the world, with almost all public services available online.

geography.text: Estonia is low and flat, with many lakes, bogs and forests. It has a long coastline on the Baltic Sea and the Gulf of Finland, and more than two thousand islands, the largest being Saaremaa and Hiiumaa. Lake Peipus, one of the largest lakes in Europe, forms much of the border with Russia.

history.text: Estonia was conquered by Danish and German crusaders in the 1200s and later ruled by Sweden and then Russia. It declared independence in 1918 but was occupied by the Soviet Union in 1940. Estonians helped end Soviet rule through peaceful mass protests, including the 'Singing Revolution', and independence was restored in 1991.

events.title: Danish conquest
events.text: Danish crusaders capture the site of Tallinn.

events.title: Russian rule
events.text: Estonia passes from Sweden to the Russian Empire.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Estonia declares itself an independent republic.

events.title: Soviet occupation
events.text: The Soviet Union occupies and annexes Estonia.

events.title: Independence restored
events.text: Estonia regains its independence as Soviet rule collapses.

government.text: Estonia is a parliamentary republic. The Riigikogu, its parliament, is elected every four years and chooses the Prime Minister. The President is elected by parliament or by a special electoral body. Estonia was the first country to let people vote online in a national election, in 2007.

economy.text: Estonia has become one of Europe's most digital countries. Almost every government service is online, and its e-Residency scheme lets people around the world start an Estonian company. Skype was built by Estonian programmers, and the money-transfer company Wise was founded by Estonians. Forestry, manufacturing and IT are key industries.

culture.text: Song and choirs are central to Estonian identity. The Song Festival, held every five years, gathers tens of thousands of singers, and singing at mass gatherings helped Estonia regain independence. Much of the country is covered in forest and bog.

items.title: Song Festival
items.text: Held since 1869; up to 30,000 singers perform together on one stage.

items.title: Tallinn Old Town
items.text: One of the best-preserved medieval towns in northern Europe.

items.title: Saunas
items.text: Smoke sauna traditions in Võromaa are listed by UNESCO.

sport.text: Basketball, football and cross-country skiing are popular in Estonia. The country has produced Olympic champions in decathlon and discus, and the rally driver Ott Tänak became world champion in 2019.

didYouKnow: Estonia was the first country to allow online voting in a national election, in 2007.
About half of Estonia is covered in forest.
